items.title: Globe-Trotter and YOSHIROTTEN Split a “SUPERNOVA” Across Three Suitcases
items.summary:
Summary 

Globe-Trotter and YOSHIROTTEN have built a three-piece suitcase set that forms one continuous artwork when the cases stand side by sideThe graphics draw from YOSHIROTTEN’s “SUPERNOVA” work, layering nebula blues, oranges, pinks and greens over the brand’s signature black fiberboardThe release commemorates the artist’s 'BEYOND EARTH' exhibition, currently on view at TOKYO NODE in Tokyo’s Toranomon Hills

Globe-Trotter has teamed up with Tokyo-based artist YOSHIROTTEN on the “SUPERNOVA” suitcase set, a limited trio of hard-shell cases that only reveals its full image when all three pieces are lined up together. Created to mark YOSHIROTTEN’s BEYOND EARTH exhibition, the project translates his large-scale cosmic imagery onto a functional travel object, turning a matching luggage set into a single, modular canvas.

Each case starts from Globe-Trotter’s defining material , a black vulcanized fiberboard shell that serves as the dark backdrop for YOSHIROTTEN’s palette. Over that base, the artist stacks bands of blue, orange, pink and green meant to evoke drifting nebulae and distant horizon lines, pulling directly from “SUPERNOVA,” his piece exploring the dramatic life cycles of stars. Because the composition runs continuously across all three shells, no single suitcase tells the whole story, which is why the cases are sold strictly as a set rather than individually.

The hardware details lean into longevity. Handles are cut from natural leather that gradually darkens into a rich amber tone with use, so every set will develop its own patina depending on how often it…
items.t: Globe-Trotter and YOSHIROTTEN Split a “SUPERNOVA” Across Three Suitcases

This month, Sotheby’s is presenting The Human Touch , a special exhibition spotlighting the enduring value of handcraftsmanship across the global luxury ecosystem. Bringing together a curated mix of rare automobiles, watches, jewelry and collectibles, the showcase celebrates the human ingenuity and technical mastery behind some of the most sought-after creations on the market in an era increasingly shaped by automation.

Leading the presentation is the coveted Hermès Mini Kelly Picnic, a standout example of artisanal savoir-faire that pairs a hand-woven natural wicker body with smooth pale blue-gray leather across its top flap, handle, and signature sangles, finished with silver-tone turn-lock hardware.

Anchoring the exhibition’s automotive narrative is British marque Morgan Motor Company , celebrated for over a century of bespoke coachbuilding that blends traditional hand-built techniques with contemporary engineering. Headlining its presence is the one-of-a-kind Morgan Midsummer Coupé “The Artists’ Proof,” showcasing sweeping sculpted fenders, a classic vertical-slat grille, and a sleek enclosed cabin finished in a deep, dark metallic hue.

items.title: Jamie Pearl on the Art of Photographing Fame
items.summary:
Summary 

Jamie Pearl reflects on capturing candid moments with Doechii, Dennis Rodman, Nina Dobrev and other cultural figures.From spontaneous celebrity portraits to experimental editorial work, the photographer shares a creative approach shaped by energy, instinct and authenticity.

Some of the most memorable celebrity photographs happen when no one's quite ready for the camera. A cigarette break outside a Fashion Week dinner, a fleeting moment in the backseat of a car, or the final touches before a red carpet appearance can reveal more personality than a carefully staged portrait. For New York-based photographer Jamie Pearl , those in-between moments have become the foundation of a practice rooted in spontaneity and human connection.

After discovering black-and-white film photography in high school, Jamie eventually found a footing in New York's fashion and entertainment circles, capturing everyone from Dennis Rodman and Doechii to Keke Palmer and Nina Dobrev. While the fast-paced world of celebrity events has sharpened an instinct for the unexpected, a growing interest in editorial photography has opened up new possibilities for creative experimentation. 

We caught up with Jamie to discuss memorable encounters, the art of thinking on your feet, and why the best images often happen when you least expect them.

"In the words of one of my favorite photographers, Tyrell Hampton, it’s all about energy." 

How did you first get into photography, and when did you start shooting celebrities?

Summary 

Artist Barry McGee has unveiled a new "solo" exhibition at Jeffrey Deitch's Los Angeles outpost, titled 'Another Round'The exhibition, running through January 30, 2027, features over 200 paintings, sculptures, and photographs by McGee alongside hundreds of works from friends and collaborators, including a mini fabrication of '99CENTS,' his knockout anti-art fair presentation earlier this year

After he opened a knockout 99CENT in February, artist Barry McGee is back in Los Angeles for Another Round , his new exhibition at Jeffrey Deitch 's Santa Monica Boulevard space. The graffiti writer-turned contemporary art star gathers over 200 paintings, sculptures, and photographs to envelope the space. It's his first show with Deitch in 20 years, and in the spirit of the Frieze anti-fair, was made possible with a little help from his friends.

While billed as such, the show is less of a “solo” than a snapshot of McGee's place in the art world: his curatorial style and unique place in high-low culture. “In this day and age, a solo anything seems ridiculous,” he recently told The Los Angeles Times. “The ego of the artist is a tricky thing.”

Highlights include a bulbous hang of prints and photographs oozing from the walls of the main gallery and kaleidoscopic tiled works peppered throughout. Crowded between them are works by the likes of CHITO , Chris Lux, Todd James , Tom Franco, C. R. Stecky III, and more, like a painted bench by Alfonzo Gonzalez Jr. and KATSU 's incognito tagger, a robotic arm spraying from the inside of a bush.

items.title: Culture Over Couture: Why Luxury is Doubling Down on Streetwear
items.summary:
To understand why European luxury fashion houses are frantically reverting to "buzzy" logos, viral collaborations, and streetwear architects, we have to look past the runway and into the balance sheets. The recent game of creative director musical chairs, which saw Martine Rose appointed as Balenciaga 's new creative director following Pierpaolo Piccioli 's brief 16 months stint, is not just a shift in aesthetic taste—it is a defensive maneuver against a severe macroeconomic reality.

People are simply not buying luxury like they used to. In 2026 alone, Europe’s top luxury conglomerates had roughly $350 billion USD wiped from their market value amid a prolonged spending slowdown, heavily driven by a pullback in the Chinese market and the evaporation of aspirational shoppers. When consumption power plummets, quiet luxury doesn't pay the bills; brands need massive cultural noise to stimulate a stagnant market.

The Attention Economy: Instant Cool Over Quiet Heritage This economic reality is compounded by a fundamental shift in how technology has rewired our consumption behavior. With infinite information at our fingertips, consumer attention spans have been severely fractured by the algorithmic churn of TikTok and Instagram. In this hyper-connected ecosystem, trends live and die at breakneck speeds, and the traditional six-month fashion calendar feels painfully slow to a consumer conditioned by the feed. Today's audience is perpetually chasing "the cool"—and they demand it immediately.

Consequently, traditional brand "heritage" is losing its standalone currency. Heritage…
items.t: Culture Over Couture: Why Luxury is Doubling Down on Streetwear

items.title: doublet Turns Your Most Used Emojis Into a Bag for FW26
items.summary:
Summary 

doublet’s FW26 "EMOJI LEATHER BAG" features 3D cowhide emoji expressions.The design physicalizes unseen human emotions to lighten emotional weight.It releases November 9 for approx. $860 USD at select retailers.

Masayuki Ino ’s doublet has always thrived on humor and subversion, turning the mundane into the unexpected. For its Fall/Winter 2026 collection, the brand taps into everyday emojis and turns them into something you can wear with the EMOJI LEATHER BAG.

The playful design stems from a longstanding adage: bags that look like faces sell well. doublet took the saying literally, utilizing intricate leather patching and precise stitching to recreate three emoji expressions in three dimensions across the front of the bags. The available expressions include the crying-laughing face, the pleading face, and the green vomiting face.

Crafted from soft cowhide leather, the tote balances its loud exterior with practical, everyday utility. Equipped with a detachable shoulder strap, allowing the wearer to effortlessly switch between hand-carry and crossbody styling.

Beyond its immediate visual punchline, the design carries a deeper meaning. doublet finds that human emotions are inherently invisible. The brand wants to explore how, by boldly wearing these unseen feelings as a physical object, the wearer could reduce the emotional weight they carry and make them feel lighter.

Available in Camel and Black, the doublet EMOJI LEATHER BAG releases on November 9, available for ¥137,500 JPY (approx. $860 USD) at doublet’s online store , and select retailers in Japan.

items.title: Toyota Is Finally Bringing a Kei Truck to America, but It Tops Out at 25 MPH
items.summary:
Summary 

Toyota is reviving the Scion brand to launch the miniature KEI-01 pickup truck in the United States in late 2027Measuring just over 11 feet long with a 660cc engine and four-wheel drive, the right-hand-drive truck tops out at 25 mph under federal low-speed vehicle rulesAssembled in Indiana, the KEI-01 will initially launch through a limited pilot program for fleet customers via selected dealers

Toyota is bringing Japan’s miniature pickup culture stateside with the new KEI-01, a compact utility truck launching under the revived Scion brand in the second half of 2027. Reintroduced a decade after its discontinuation around the “freedom to explore mobility in new ways,” Scion will debut the pint-sized truck as a practical alternative to full-size American pickups.

Measuring just over 11 feet long and under five feet wide, the right-hand-drive KEI-01 is powered by a 660cc three-cylinder gasoline engine paired with an automatic transmission and selectable four-wheel drive. Despite its compact footprint, the truck hauls up to 600 pounds in a three-way fold-down cargo bed and can tow small trailers. Inside the enclosed extended cabin, drivers get heating, air conditioning, sliding and reclining seats, and rear storage for tools. To meet federal low-speed vehicle safety regulations, however, the truck tops out at 25 mph—restricting it in many states to roads with speed limits of 35 mph or less.

Backed by a $34 million USD investment creating roughly 50 jobs, assembly will begin at Toyota’s Indiana factory in the second half of 2027.

items.title: Theaster Gates Recasts Tar, Clay and Gym Floors for His Hong Kong Exhibition ‘Surrogate’
items.summary:
Summary 

Theaster Gates revisits his signature motifs in ‘Surrogate,’ transferring them onto new materials or setting them in fresh compositionsThe show includes fire-hose imprints in clay, reclaimed gymnasium flooring, a clay “handbag” and a trio of new Tar PaintingsThe exhibition explores how art can stand in for something absent, whether a family bond, a community or a history that has been overlooked

Theaster Gates brings Surrogate , an exhibition of new works, to Gagosian Hong Kong from November 19. The show finds the Chicago-based artist mining his own visual language, lifting elements from earlier series and reworking them through different materials and arrangements. Each piece is built on the idea that an artwork can act on behalf of something that isn’t there, a thread that has run through Gates’ practice for more than a decade.

Fire hoses offer the clearest example of that material shift. Gates has used decommissioned hoses since 2011 in his Civil Tapestries, flat, striped compositions that call up the hoses turned on civil rights protesters. For Surrogate , he presses those same hoses into slabs of clay, so the ridged texture once read as fabric and paint now sits in fired ceramic surfaces.

A similar reworking happens with his “gym floor” pieces, a series he started in 2014 using varnished planks salvaged from school gymnasiums. Rather than leaving the court lines in their original layout, Gates has reorganized the painted markings into graphic bands. The new geometry echoes a set of paintings he made in the late 2010s, which drew on the data visualizations…
items.t: Theaster Gates Recasts Tar, Clay and Gym Floors for His Hong Kong Exhibition ‘Surrogate’

items.title: ‘GTA VII’ Outside America? Rockstar Won’t Rule It Out
items.summary:
Summary 

Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson has declined to rule out a ‘Grand Theft Auto’ game set outside the US, though he stopped short of confirming any plansThe comments land as ‘GTA VI’ prepares to launch with what is described as the series’ most detailed recreation of America to dateRockstar has weighed overseas settings before, with a shelved ‘GTA: Tokyo’ concept and pitches spanning Rio de Janeiro, Moscow, Istanbul, London and Paris

Grand Theft Auto may not be bound to American soil forever, with Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson signaling that an international setting remains possible for the franchise. Speaking with The Guardian ahead of GTA VI ’s launch, Nelson was asked whether Rockstar could picture a mainline entry outside the US. His answer left room for it, though he did not reference a specific sequel or commit to any destination.

Nelson’s full response was brief and carefully balanced. “Never say never, but there’s still so much to do in America,” he told The Guardian . The line keeps the series’ home turf firmly in focus while acknowledging that a departure is not off limits. Any talk of a GTA VII setting remains speculation, since Rockstar has yet to formally announce a follow-up.

The scale of what Rockstar builds helps explain the caution. GTA VI returns players to Vice City , the studio’s fictional stand-in for Miami, and expands outward into the surrounding state of Leonida. The game has spent more than a decade in development and is billed as the franchise’s most detailed take on America yet, which sets an enormous bar for any…

items.title: Jess Cartner-Morley on fashion: this season’s big idea? Wear a skirt. It’s that simple
items.summary:
All you need to look on-trend this autumn is a skirt, but instead of going shopping, check what you already have in your wardrobe

I go to a lot of fashion shows, and sometimes they are gorgeous and sometimes they are ugly. Sometimes they are electrifying and sometimes they are deathly dull. Sometimes they are completely baffling. My absolute favourite kind of show is the one that makes me want to run home and change my outfit. A show that makes me think: there it is! That’s exactly what I want to wear. When the look speaks to me, as if it had been on the tip of my tongue. God, I love that.

Which is what happened at Prada this season. The idea was: skirts. That’s it, that’s the whole idea. The show was 63 different skirts – some with a sweater, some with a bra top, some with a jacket, but the point was the skirts. They were knee-length, give or take an inch up or down, and A-line, although sometimes a narrow almost-pencil and other times with a broader flare. There were skirts that wrapped like kilts, held together with strips of industrial-weight Velcro embroidered with tiny gems. There were stiff boxy pleated skirts and tube skirts painted with swirls, and dainty embellished skirts with a layer of gauze on top, like a petticoat worn on the outside.
